newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HORN PROMISES TOUGH ACTION IN WAKE OF APV SCANDAL.
newsitem.headline: HORN PROMISES TOUGH ACTION IN WAKE OF APV SCANDAL.

text.p: Hungarian Prime Minister Gyula Horn on Thursday promised tough action to stamp out corruption in state-run agencies in the wake of the privatisation scandal which forced him to sack his industry and trade minister.
"Society must come together to fight corruption," he told Hungarian Television, adding that anti-corruption agencies will be strengthened.

Horn said the new leadership of the state privatisation agency APV would ensure that there would be no repeat of the so-called "Tocsik scandal" in which a consultant Marta Tocsik was paid 804 million forints ($5.2 million) for negotiating compensation deals for APV with local authorities.

Horn, in an announcement on Wednesday night, said he was appointing Judit Csiha as minister in charge of the state privatisation agency APV to replace Tamas Suchman and Arpad Kovacs for president of the APV board of directors and Andras Laszlo as APV general manager to replace Imre Szokai and Istvan Kocsis.
"These three will ensure that laws are respected," he said.
